scope: non-Mundarica source census; peer-reviewed article, interview/video-derived linguistic evidence, narrative/song material

canonical_source.author: Nishaant Choksi
canonical_source.title: Expressives and the multimodal depiction of social types in Mundari

verified_exact_locators.supported_source_fact: The article states that Mundari data came from a two-year Japan-India collaborative project and that discussions were video recorded to capture multimodality.

verified_exact_locators.locator: DATA AND METHODS; paragraph beginning 'Following the initial data elicitation sessions'
verified_exact_locators.supported_source_fact: The article describes a two-week field trip to a village in Khunti district, Jharkhand and identifies the speakers there as native speakers of the Hasada variety of Mundari.

verified_exact_locators.locator: DATA AND METHODS; paragraph beginning 'As part of the field session in the village'
verified_exact_locators.supported_source_fact: The article describes Mundari elicitation with Madhu Purti and family members and states that the elicitations were conducted in Mundari and video-recorded.
The article distinguishes four major Mundari varieties and discusses expressive morphology/syntax, while attributing relevant linguistic background to cited upstream works.

rights_and_ethics.notes: The shared Cambridge manifestation supports exact section-level external locators and source/provenance auditing. It does not establish permission to copy underlying interview video, transcripts, song material, participant likeness/voice, or culturally sensitive content into MLHKP.

deduplication.canonicalization_rule: Cambridge abstract page, shared/read-only article view, DOI resolver, bibliographic indexes and author/institutional listings are manifestations/metadata for one article identity, not independent corroborating sources.
upstream_dependencies: Osada et al. 2019 and other works cited for lexical/grammatical background
deduplication.underlying_fieldwork: Interview/video sessions described in the article are underlying primary research material and must not be multiplied into independent evidence identities without member-level provenance and permissions.
